A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LLM-VA and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G. Content can be matched across the changed pagination and figure placement.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on 12 LLMs, utility measurements, component ablations, and transferability experiments in Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations and reports revised values in the layer-selection ablation.

M1.justification: SVM vector identification, layer scoring, iterative re-extraction, and the closed-form weight update remain unchanged. v2 adds stopping-patience documentation, but does not establish that the underlying alignment procedure was changed rather than described more fully.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four primary safety datasets, six utility datasets, and five transferability benchmarks. The new Section 5.5 summarizes experiments already present in v1 Appendix G.

E2.justification: The corresponding experimental comparisons retain Original, VectorSteer, AlphaSteer, AlphaSteer+, and SCANS. Tables 2 and 4 contain the same comparator sets; additional citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The stated sample selection, 8:1:1 splits, model configurations, metrics, judge model, and maximum of 30 iterations are retained. The newly specified early-stopping patience is additional implementation documentation; the PDFs do not establish a changed experimental protocol or rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 8 revises the Qwen3-14B layer-selection ablation, shifting its plotted F1 peak from 36 to 48 selected layers. Other ablation questions and the appendix transferability analyses remain. The new adversarial-robustness discussion adds no attack experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose single-run results with fixed seed 42 and acknowledge the absence of statistical significance testing. No repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals, or other uncertainty procedures are added.

E6.justification: In Figure 8, Qwen3-14B's plotted F1 changes from approximately 0.71 to 0.86 at 48 selected layers and from 0.69 to 0.84 at 54 layers. The reason is not explained. Main benchmark results in Table 2 and transferability results in Table 4 remain identical.

T1.justification: The optimization objective, SVM formulation, layer scores, and weight-update derivation in Equations 1–9 are unchanged. Added geometric and training-based explanations do not introduce a formal theorem, proof, or revised mathematical definition.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same alignment claim, absence of fine-tuning or architectural changes, automatic adaptation claim, and reported 11.45% F1 improvement with 95.92% utility preservation.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting vector independence to separately optimized safety objectives, SVMs to outlier robustness, and transfer difficulties to inconsistent benchmark safety definitions. Section 7 adds a specific limitation concerning adversarial manipulation of the safety representation. These interpretations receive no new dedicated validation.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 newly specifies early stopping after three consecutive iterations without validation-F1 improvement; the 30-iteration ceiling was already documented. v2 also removes the review-stage weight-release footnote and direct Figshare link while retaining the project-site link.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Pandora, Lockpicking LLMs, a cross-language jailbreak investigation, and DeepSeek-R1. These extend the attack background and training-based explanation, while the central positioning against existing steering methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 expands several explanatory paragraphs, introduces RQ4 and a main-text transferability subsection, and adds acknowledgements. It also updates an affiliation and email ordering. Most prose and the overall section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 expands from one Gemma plot to four model panels using coverage already available in Appendix A. Several plots receive revised labels, legends, fonts, or ticks, and figures and tables reflow across pages. The overall document design and table structures remain stable.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves readability and implementation transparency through clearer plots and explicit stopping patience, while making transferability and adaptive-attack limitations more concrete. These gains are limited: the main empirical evidence is unchanged, the Figure 8 revision is unexplained, and removal of the direct weights link reduces access detail.
